draft.title: Specialised cells, tissues and organs
card: In many-celled organisms, cells take on special shapes for special jobs. This is called specialisation. A specialised cell has a structure that suits its job.
long and thin, with branches at the ends. This shape helps it carry messages around the body.
small and disc-shaped, and it carries oxygen around the body in the blood.
A group of similar cells that do the same job is a tissue, such as muscle tissue. Different tissues working together form an organ, such as the heart or the stomach.
draft.remember: Cells are specialised for a job, similar cells make a tissue, and different tissues make an organ.

opts: A group of similar cells that do the same job
A single cell with a special shape
A group of organs that work together
A cell that carries messages around the body
a.why: A tissue is made of many similar cells doing the same job. A single specialised cell is not a tissue, because a tissue is a group of cells. Organs are made of tissues, not the other way around.
a.clue: Think about how many cells there are, and how alike they are.

b.q: Dani reads that the stomach has muscle tissue, gland tissue and other tissues that work together to digest food. What is the stomach?
opts: An organ, because it is made of different tissues
A tissue, because it is made of many cells
A specialised cell, because it has one job
A tissue, because all its cells look the same
b.why: The stomach is made of different tissues working together, so it is an organ. It is not a tissue, because a tissue is made of similar cells and the stomach has more than one kind of tissue.
b.clue: Count how many kinds of tissue the stomach has.

a.best: A group of similar cells that do the same job

b.best: An organ, because it is made of different tissues
